channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Cardinals ruled out Carson Beck (back) for Week 11 against the Chiefs.
item.description: That paves the way for 36-year-old journeyman quarterback Josh Johnson to draw the start under center for the Cardinals after being added to the team less than two weeks ago. Dynasty managers will be forced to wait longer for the first extended look at the third-round rookie as the Cardinals continue forward with insurmountable injuries up and down their roster in what has quickly become a lost season. Downgrade the primary skill position players in a difficult matchup against the Chiefs in Week 11.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Titans placed RB Tyjae Spears (knee) on injured reserve.
item.description: Spears will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he tends to a knee injury that has plagued him in recent weeks. Spears previously missed two games in Week 7 and Week 8 before returning to a modest workload in Week 9 after the team’s bye. Tony Pollard should continue operating in a true workhorse role and gets one of the top matchups in the league against the Cowboys in Week 11. Fantasy managers can continue to treat Pollard as a volume-driven RB1 after a slow start to the season.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Commanders HC Dan Quinn told reporters RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is “trending the right way” ahead of the matchup with the Bengals in Week 11.
item.description: Quinn said Croskey-Merritt had a great week and is trending the right way for Monday’s game against the Bengals. It’s great news for fantasy managers and the Commanders as backup running back Rachaad White (heel) missed practice Saturday. Croskey-Merritt deserves FLEX consideration assuming he’s active against the Bengals this week.-Nick Shlain

item.title: Rachaad White (heel) missed practice on Saturday.
item.description: White was added to the injury report and was a limited participant in practice on Friday. His missed practice Saturday is another bad sign for the 27-year-old running back’s availability. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) trending towards being available, White doesn’t seem to have much fantasy value at the moment. CB Amik Robertson, who was seen limping in the locker room on Friday, also missed practice Saturday.-Nick Shlain

item.title: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Titans WR Carnell Tate (shoulder) is likely to return against the Cowboys in Week 11.
item.description: Tate hasn’t played since Week 7 due to a shoulder injury. Still officially questionable, Zenitz reports Tate is likely to play in Week 11. While he’s been out for over a month, Tate got in a full practice on Friday. He’ll be a high-end WR3 in a plus matchup against the brutal Cowboys defense.-Nick Shlain

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield (foot) is dealing with a plantar fascia injury.
item.description: While Mayfield remains on track to play against the Lions on Sunday, he’s dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury, according to Pelissero. If the 31-year-old gunslinger suits up in Week 11, he’ll wear a special orthotic and new cleats to help stabilize his foot. Mayfield looked doubtful to play earlier in the week and even missed practice Wednesday before getting in a pair of limited sessions. Jalon Daniels would start if Mayfield isn’t able to play this week.-Nick Shlain

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler described Rams WR Puka Nacua’s future with the team as “very uncertain.”
item.description: Nothing earth-shattering here from Fowler. Appearing on ESPN’s SportsCenter Saturday morning, the NFL Insider noted that Nacua is dealing with a significant MCL injury and a three-game suspension from the NFL. With Nacua unlikely to return this season, Fowler says this isn’t the kind of momentum the 25-year-old receiver wanted heading into free agency, where he’ll be the best player available. The Rams can extend him, franchise tag him or let him hit the open market this offseason. As Fowler says, it’s something the Rams have to sort out.-Nick Shlain

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Bud Dupree has requested his release from the Chargers.
item.description: Fowler also reveals that Dupree asked to be released in the offseason, but the Chargers have been unwilling to grant it. Dupree is playing infrequently and has just two quarterback pressures and one tackle. Releasing him would reduce their depth, but he is not a critical defender for this 1-8 squad. Stay tuned.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Mike Evans (Achilles) “is trending in the right direction” for Week 11 against the Vikings.
item.description: Rapoport does note, however, that Evans is “a little sore” after returning to practice on Thursday. The 49ers will make a decision on Evans’ Week 11 status on Saturday. If active, Evans will carry some re-injury risk, but reports have consistently indicated that the 49ers learned a lot from Christian McCaffrey’s bilateral Achilles tendinitis in 2024. It seems safe to assume that if Evans is active, his Achilles tendon is in good shape. Evans may not immediately return to his pre-injury form against the Vikings’ elite defense, but he should be in fantasy football lineups.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Puka Nacua’s (knee/toe) recovery timeline “does not match up” with a potential return for Super Bowl LXI.
item.description: Nacua is currently on injured reserve, recovering from MCL and PCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury. He will also serve a three-game suspension on injured reserve, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye. The superstar wide receiver underwent surgery to repair his MCL on Tuesday, and Rapoport believes we have “almost certainly” seen the last of Nacua in the 2026 season. He is set to enter free agency this offseason, and it is unclear whether the Rams will extend him, franchise tag him or allow him to walk.-Nic Bodiford
